title: Icon Raises $200M in Series D Funding to Scale Robotic Construction Systems
key_facts: Icon raised $200 million in a Series D to expand production and rollout of its robotic construction systems, including the Titan platform.
Baillie Gifford and funds managed by BlackRock co-led the round.
Icon is based in Austin, Texas and plans a large research facility there and expansion in Texas, Florida and Washington, D.C.
Titan is a multi-story 3D-printing system; Icon says it can cut average home build time by six weeks and cost by 40%.
Icon says it has completed more than 270 homes and structures in five states and two countries.
In January it began work on 10 barracks at Fort Bliss, which it says is its largest military deployment.
Icon Prime has received more than $370 million in government contracts and works with NASA on Project Olympus for the Moon.
quote_evidence: Icon has raised $200 million in Series D financing to expand production and deployment of its robotic construction systems, including the commercial rollout of its Titan platform.
Icon said the system is designed to reduce construction of an average home by six weeks and cut costs by 40% compared with the national average.
why_it_matters_hint: Automated building is being funded as a way to ease the US housing shortage.
notes: Time and cost savings, revenue growth and project counts are Icon's own claims.
